column1: # mapping_set_title: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 to ISO/IEC 29100:2011 Privacy Framework Schema Mappings

# mapping_set_description: Schema-level mappings between the ISO/IEC 42001:2023 (AI Management System) LinkML schema and the ISO/IEC 29100:2011 (Privacy Framework) LinkML schema. ISO 29100 establishes a high-level privacy framework with eleven privacy principles, PII actor roles, and supporting concepts (PII flow scenarios, safeguarding requirements, privacy controls, PIA). The mappings bridge AI-system governance with privacy governance where ISO 42001 obligations touch personal data, AI subjects, and impact assessments.

column10: comment
Both are top-level governance containers; AI management system can incorporate the ISO 29100 privacy framework where AI systems process PII
An ISO 42001 organisation acting on PII is a PII controller under ISO 29100
An organisation may also act as a PII processor depending on the role in the PII flow
Interested parties in ISO 42001 correspond to ISO 29100 privacy stakeholders (PII principals, controllers, processors, third parties, authorities)
AI subjects whose personal data is processed are PII principals
AI partners involved in PII handling are third parties in privacy terms
Data resources used by AI systems that identify natural persons are PII
An AI policy is parallel in structure to an ISO 29100 privacy policy; both express organisational commitments and obligations
Annex A AI controls and ISO 29100 privacy controls are both safeguard catalogues
AI-system impact assessment is methodologically parallel to a PIA; both assess impacts on individuals before/during processing
Privacy risk is a sub-category of AI risk when the AI system processes PII; not equivalent
A privacy breach is a specific kind of AI incident when PII is exposed or misused
The AIIncidentCategory privacy_breach value is realised by the ISO 29100 PrivacyBreach class
Operational procedures over AI systems that touch PII record processing activities
Several ISO 42001 AI objectives mirror ISO 29100 privacy principles (privacy, accountability, transparency)
Privacy is the umbrella principle of ISO 29100
Accountability is principle 9 of ISO 29100
ISO 29100 principle 7 covers openness, transparency and notice
Information security is principle 10 of ISO 29100
Data quality aligns with ISO 29100's accuracy-and-quality principle
Fairness in AI partly relates to individual participation rights under ISO 29100
Privacy safeguarding requirements often feed into the risk-treatment plan when AI processes PII
The risk owner for a privacy risk is typically the PII controller
Identified AI risks include privacy risks
